content: Diastole refers to the phase of the cardiac cycle during which the heart muscle relaxes following contraction. Ventricular diastole specifically describes the relaxation of the ventricles, while atrial diastole pertains to the relaxation of the atria. During ventricular diastole, the pressure within the left and right ventricles decreases from the peak levels reached during systole. When the pressure in the left ventricle falls below the pressure in the left atrium, the mitral valve (also known as the bicuspid valve) opens. This allows the blood that has accumulated in the left atrium to flow into the left ventricle. The term diastolic is used to describe the relaxation phase of the heart between muscle contractions. It is often applied to specific portions of the cardiac cycle associated with relaxation and is a key component in the measurement of blood pressure. Diastolic pressure refers to the lowest pressure within the arterial blood stream during each heartbeat. In contrast, systolic pressure represents the highest arterial pressure during each heartbeat. Blood pressure is typically expressed with the systolic pressure stated first, followed by the diastolic pressure, such as in the example 120/80.
